## Document: README.md (Overview)

# @actdim/dynstruct-mui

MUI component wrappers for [@actdim/dynstruct](https://github.com/actdim/dynstruct). Each component is a dynstruct hook-constructor - observable props, reactive rendering, MobX-backed state out of the box.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@actdim/dynstruct-mui.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@actdim/dynstruct-mui)
[![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.9+-blue.svg)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)

## Installation

```bash
npm install @actdim/dynstruct-mui
```

Peer dependencies: `@actdim/dynstruct`, `@mui/material`, `react`, `mobx`, `mobx-react-lite` - see `package.json` for full list.

## Usage

```tsx
import { useButton } from '@actdim/dynstruct-mui/Button';

const saveBtn = useButton({
    props: {
        label: 'Save',
        variant: 'contained',
        onClick: () => handleSave(),
    },
});

// In JSX:
// <saveBtn.view />
// or via React adapter:
import { Button } from '@actdim/dynstruct-mui/Button';
// <Button label="Save" variant="contained" onClick={handleSave} />
```

## Development

```bash
pnpm storybook      # run Storybook
pnpm build          # build
pnpm typecheck      # type check
pnpm lint           # lint
pnpm format         # format
```

## Document: AGENTS.md (Agent Conventions & Protocol)

<!-- BEGIN ALONG-PROTOCOL root (managed by along-init - do not edit by hand) -->
# ALONG-PROTOCOL v4.5.4

This repo carries its own agent context, provider-agnostically. Follow it every session, whatever tool you are. This is the core; procedures (completion checklist, doc routing, merges, along-team, tool-use rules) live in `docs/topic--along-protocol.md` - pull the section you need via `/along-kb-search`. A gate's error message carries its detail.

## Where state lives
- **Nearest wins**: any folder may carry its own `AGENTS.md` + `.along/`; use the NEAREST for the area you work in. Nearest `.along/` > higher-level `.along/` > global config. Only a nested `.git` or a user-run `along init` makes a subproject.
- **Read at session start** (not auto-loaded): `.along/ISSUES.md`, `.along/CONSTRAINTS.md`, your issue `.along/ISSUES/<type>--<slug>.md`; when relevant `.along/VISION.md`, `.along/GLOSSARY.md`. They reflect the state WHEN WRITTEN - verify named files/APIs/flags against the code.
- **Entities**: issues (`feat|bug|debt|task|docs|spike`), ADRs (`.along/DECISIONS/`, never edited - superseded), milestones, sessions. Keys `<type>--<slug>`, referenced by key, never by path; schemas in `docs/topic--domain-model.md`. Create them from intent unprompted (build/fix -> issue, blocked -> issue tagged `risk`, compare -> `spike` issue, release -> milestone).
- **Projections** (`ISSUES.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `CONSTRAINTS.md`, `docs/INDEX.md`) are compiled: on conflict take either side and re-run the sync.

## Anchor work to an issue
1. Find or create the issue with `status: in-progress`; `along start <slug>` binds this session.
2. Source edits unlock after the user approves the plan (`EnterPlanMode` -> `ExitPlanMode`, or `along plan approve --plan-file <path>` after their explicit yes). Questions get read-only answers; 1-line typo/comment edits are exempt.
3. Commit via `/along-commit`: bound to the slug, no AI `Co-Authored-By:` trailers.
4. Finish with the completion checklist, ending in `along wrap <slug> --summary "..." (--decisions <ADR...> | --no-decisions)`.

## Gates
Runtime hooks enforce these where installed; elsewhere (`along doctor` shows the level) self-apply every one and use the `along` CLI instead of raw tools.
- [gate: require-active-issue] [gate: require-plan-approval] - no source edit without an in-progress issue and an approved plan.
- [gate: subproject-boundary] - a subproject's entities go in ITS `.along/`; cross-subproject work needs an issue in each, or a root umbrella with `parent:` children.
- [gate: workspace-containment] - read/write inside the workspace (plus temp); other roots need `allowed_roots`; never credential stores.
- [gate: projection-protection] - never hand-edit or hand-merge projections.
- [gate: commit-issue-binding] - every commit names the active issue.
- [gate: issue-lifecycle] [gate: entity-reference-integrity] [gate: entity-deletion-protection] - close via `along wrap` / `along issue done`; rename or supersede, never delete a referenced entity.
- [gate: doc-manual-lock] - `write_policy: manual` docs change only under a `docs--<slug>` issue.
- [gate: rule-pack-protection] - never edit `.along/rules/**/*.md` (`along rules attach` owns them).
- [gate: doc-routing-compliance] - ADR vs `README.md` vs `docs/topic--*.md` routing tree.
- [gate: untracked-exports] - dashboards and `.along/diagnostics/` stay out of Git.
- [gate: cli_safety] - file content via file tools, never heredocs or `python -c`; no global installs.
- [gate: team-step-active] [gate: team-reviews-before-stop] - an `along-team` blackboard holds you to its step loop.
- [gate: test_before_stop] [gate: wrap_before_stop] [gate: projection_sync_before_stop] - before stopping: tests green, session wrapped, projections synced.
- [gate: unresolved_gate_denial] - a denied tool call is redone within the gate's rules or told to the user (`along gates ack`), never dropped silently; closing waits for their reply.
- Commit-time (`along lint`, pre-commit + CI): ASCII typography, fence languages, relative links, no `docs/` -> `.along/` links, Windows-safe names, no secrets, no stubs.
- Bypass is the user's call: `-n`, `--force-reason`, `scratch fallback` need `--reason` after their reply; recorded in `along gates stats`.

## Judgment rules
- Ground facts in code, `README.md` and `docs/`; no generic placeholders. Query `/along-kb-search` before reading whole docs; update affected `docs/topic--*.md` after non-trivial changes.
- Use `/along-test`, `/along-build`, `/along-dev` before raw commands, with quiet flags. Review your diff and blast radius (`along graph-impact`).
- Never delete or truncate docs, comments or code unless told; no stubs; check `git diff --stat` after batch edits. Verify written files parse. Tests stay hermetic.
- Scope > 3 files, crossing subsystems or refactoring core engines: route to `along-team`; plans MUST declare `Execution Mode: Direct` or `Role-Based`.
- Treat the `along` CLI as a black box (`along <cmd> --help`, no engine source outside the Along repo); report its errors verbatim.
<!-- END ALONG-PROTOCOL -->

# AI Agent Guide for `@actdim/dynstruct-mui`

MUI wrappers for `@actdim/dynstruct`. Each file wraps one MUI component into a dynstruct hook-constructor.

## Tech Stack

- TypeScript · React · MobX · `@actdim/dynstruct` · `@mui/material` · Vite

## Component Authoring Pattern

Every component follows this exact structure (see `src/Button.tsx` as the reference):

```tsx
import { type ComponentStruct, type ComponentDef, type ComponentParams,
         type Component, type ComponentModel } from '@actdim/dynstruct/componentModel/contracts';
import { useComponent, toReact } from '@actdim/dynstruct/componentModel/react/hooks';
import { type BaseAppMsgStruct } from '@actdim/dynstruct/appDomain/appContracts';

// 1. Local Struct type - generic but private to file, default = BaseAppMsgStruct
type Struct<TMsgStruct extends BaseAppMsgStruct = BaseAppMsgStruct> = ComponentStruct<
    TMsgStruct,
    {
        props: { /* ... */ };
    }
>;

// 2. Hook-constructor - NOT generic, uses Struct with default
export const useXxx = (params: ComponentParams<Struct>): Component<Struct> => {
    let c: Component<Struct>;
    let m: ComponentModel<Struct>;

    const def: ComponentDef<Struct> = {
        regType: 'Xxx',
        props: { /* defaults */ },
        view: () => ( /* JSX using m.* and m.$.* */ ),
    };

    c = useComponent(def, params);
    m = c.model;
    return c;
};

// 3. Exported type - concrete (non-generic) alias
export type XxxStruct = Struct;

// 4. React adapter - no explicit type params needed
export const Xxx = toReact(useXxx);
Xxx.displayName = 'Xxx';
```

### Rules

- **`Struct` stays local** - generic with `TMsgStruct` default, never exported directly.
- **Hook-constructor is non-generic** - `useXxx(params: ComponentParams<Struct>): Component<Struct>`.
- **`XxxStruct` export is non-generic** - `export type XxxStruct = Struct`.
- **`toReact` needs no type params** - `toReact(useXxx)` works because the hook is non-generic.
- **`displayName`** - always set `Xxx.displayName = 'Xxx'` after `toReact(...)` so Storybook and React DevTools show the correct name.
- **Disabled state** - use `m.$.isDisabled` (from `ComponentState`), not a dedicated `disabled` prop.
- **Loading state** - use explicit `loading?: boolean` prop or wire to `m.$.pendingRequestCount > 0`.
- **`m.$.isVisible`** - hide/show via component state, not a prop.

## Consuming Wrappers (priority)

Inside a dynstruct component, use a wrapper as a **child**, not as inline JSX:

```tsx
import { useDialog, type DialogStruct } from '@actdim/dynstruct-mui/Dialog';
import { bindProp } from '@actdim/dynstruct/componentModel/core';

// struct: children: { addDialog: DialogStruct }
children: {
    addDialog: useDialog({
        open: bindProp(() => m, 'addDialogOpen'),
    }),
},
view: () => <c.children.AddDialog />,
```

- Import the hook-constructor and struct (`useXxx`, `XxxStruct`), declare the child in `children`, render `<c.children.Xxx />`.
- Bind values with `bindProp(() => m, 'prop')` first; use `bind(get, set)` only when the getter/setter needs specific logic.
- The `toReact` export (`Xxx`) is for plain React code and backward compatibility only - do not render `<Xxx prop={m.value} ... />` inline in a dynstruct `view`.
- Full rules: `@actdim/dynstruct` AGENTS.md, "Composition and Performance Rules" and "Binding priority".

## Import Paths

```ts
// Contracts (types only)
import { ... } from '@actdim/dynstruct/componentModel/contracts';

// React utilities (useComponent, toReact)
import { ... } from '@actdim/dynstruct/componentModel/react/hooks';
//                                                     ^^^^^^^^^^^
// Note: the file lives at dist/componentModel/react/react.d.ts
// NOT dist/componentModel/react.d.ts - that file does not exist

// App domain
import { ... } from '@actdim/dynstruct/appDomain/appContracts';
import { ... } from '@actdim/dynstruct/appDomain/commonContracts';
```

## MUI Composition Rules

Always follow the **official MUI website patterns** - use composable building blocks, not convenience shorthands:

| Component | Correct pattern |
|---|---|
| Select | `FormControl` + `InputLabel` + `Select` + `FormHelperText` |
| Checkbox (with label/error) | `FormControl` + `FormControlLabel` wrapping `Checkbox` + `FormHelperText` |
| Switch (with label/error) | `FormControl` + `FormControlLabel` wrapping `Switch` + `FormHelperText` |
| TextField | `TextField` (this IS the official atomic component, not a shorthand) |
| Button / IconButton | Use directly |
| Dialog | `Dialog` + `DialogTitle` + `DialogContent` + `DialogActions` |
| Alert | `Alert` directly (`onClose` for close button) |

- **`disabled`** always goes on the outermost container (`FormControl`, `Button`, etc.) - not inside, not as a duplicate.
- **`error`** and **`helperText`** always use `FormControl error={}` + `FormHelperText` - not ad-hoc inline text.
- **`sx`** type: when `FormControl` is the root, use `FormControlProps['sx']`, otherwise `MuiXxxProps['sx']`.
- For `labelId` (Select, etc.) use `c.id` from the dynstruct component instance to ensure uniqueness.

## Props Convention

- Map MUI prop types via `MuiXxxProps['propName']` - e.g. `MuiButtonProps['variant']`.
- Include `sx?` typed from the **outermost MUI element** (see MUI Composition Rules above).
- React content props (`ReactNode`, `React.FC`, component types: icons, titles, slots, `children`) are declared with `prop({ reactive: 'ref' })` from `@actdim/dynstruct/componentModel/core`, keeping a non-`undefined` default via `initialValue` (`children: prop({ initialValue: () => null, reactive: 'ref' })`). Without it a value assigned after creation gets deep reactivity and MobX converts the React value, which breaks rendering when a debugger is attached. React values nested in item arrays (`items: [{ icon: <Icon /> }]`) are not covered by this.
- Provide sensible defaults for all props in `def.props`.

## Storybook Stories

Every story file uses `AppContextProvider` + `StorageService` as the decorator. See `src/_stories/Button.stories.tsx` as the reference.

```tsx
import { AppContextProvider, appMsgBus } from './bootstrap';
import { StorageService } from '@actdim/dynstruct/services/react/StorageService';

const meta: Meta<typeof Xxx> = {
    title: 'Controls/Xxx',
    component: Xxx,
    decorators: [
        (Story) => (
            <AppContextProvider value={{ msgBus: appMsgBus }}>
                <StorageService storeName={'test'} />
                <Story />
            </AppContextProvider>
        ),
    ],
    // ...
};
```

- Always use `Meta<typeof Xxx>` explicit annotation (not `satisfies`) - avoids TS2742 from pnpm MUI path references.
- `argTypes` for `startIcon`, `endIcon`, `sx`: set `control: false` (not Storybook-controllable).
- `FullWidth` story should use `parameters: { layout: 'padded' }`.

## File Layout

```
src/
  Button.tsx            ← one file per MUI component
  TextField.tsx
  ...
  _stories/
    bootstrap.ts        ← AppMsgStruct, appMsgBus, AppContextProvider
    Button.stories.tsx
    ...
```

Import from the package: `import { useButton, ButtonStruct } from '@actdim/dynstruct-mui/Button'`.

## Document: docs/topic--along-protocol.md (Along Protocol Reference)

<!-- ALONG-PROTOCOL-REFERENCE (managed by along-init - do not edit by hand) -->

# Along Protocol Reference

The managed block in `AGENTS.md` is the always-loaded core of the ALONG-PROTOCOL: where state lives, how work is anchored to an issue, and the list of gates. This article carries the situational procedure the core points to. Pull the section you need with `/along-kb-search` instead of reading the whole file. `along init` and `along update` regenerate this file from the installed protocol; repository-specific guidance belongs in its own `docs/topic--<slug>.md` article or in `AGENTS.md` "Project specifics".

## Scope, Precedence & Subproject Placement

- **Nearest Context Boundary**: Any folder may carry its own `AGENTS.md` + `.along/`; use the NEAREST ones for the area you're working in. On conflict, the more specific wins.
- **Subproject Localization** [gate: subproject-boundary]: In submodules, nested repos or symlinked folders: all entities (issues, sessions, ADRs, history) MUST be created in the NEAREST `.along/`. Agents are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN from dumping subproject changes into the workspace root `.along/`.
- **Multi-Subproject Work** [gate: subproject-boundary]: A change spanning subprojects needs an issue in each touched `.along/`, or a root umbrella issue whose child issues there carry `parent: <umbrella key>`. Edits under a subproject `.along/` are checked by path.
- **Subproject Boundary**: only a nested `.git` or a user-run `along init` makes a subproject; never init a manifest folder.
- **Precedence**: Nearest `.along/` > higher-level `.along/` > global config (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, `~/.gemini/config/GEMINI.md`).

## Session Start

Use the NEAREST `.along/` for the area you're working in (fall back to a higher-level one if the folder has none). These files are NOT auto-loaded; read them yourself:

1. `AGENTS.md` (nearest) - conventions to follow.
2. `.along/ISSUES.md` - active issue board (or query `/along-kb-search`).
3. `.along/CONSTRAINTS.md` - active architectural constraints (or full log in `.along/DECISIONS.md` / `.along/DECISIONS/`).
4. Active Issue file `.along/ISSUES/<type>--<slug>.md` for your task.

Also, when relevant: `.along/VISION.md`, `.along/GLOSSARY.md`. These reflect the state WHEN WRITTEN - verify any named file/API/flag against the real code first.

## Multi-Agent & Multi-Branch Concurrency

- **Zero-Manual-Merge Rule** [gate: projection-protection]: On merge conflicts in derived projections (`ISSUES.md`, `INDEX.md`, `DECISIONS.md`), accept either side and run `/along-issue-sync`, `/along-kb-sync`, or `/along-decision-sync` to recompile. `along git setup` registers merge drivers that do this automatically; afterwards run `along git sync`.
- **Append-Only Merge Driver**: `.along/HISTORY.md` and legacy monolithic `.along/DECISIONS.md` are append-only. Configure `.gitattributes` with `merge=union`. Modular ADR files in `.along/DECISIONS/` are isolated per-file to eliminate merge collisions.
- **Untracked Exports** [gate: untracked-exports]: `.along/dashboard.html`, `.along/DASHBOARD.md` and per-machine `.along/diagnostics/` stay out of Git.
- **Context Isolation**: Context is localized to the target issue file, session-scoped blackboard (`.along/.session/<slug>/`), and completed session logs.
- **Parallel Closeout**: `along session list`; on the user's yes `along plan approve --closeout --ready`, then `along session close --ready`.

## Issue Anchoring & Commits

- **No Code Without Issue** [gate: require-active-issue]: Before modifying source code, agents MUST identify or create an issue in `.along/ISSUES/<type>--<slug>.md` and set `status: in-progress`.
- **Session Binding & Plan Approval** [gate: require-plan-approval]: `along start <slug>` binds THIS agent session to the issue; parallel sessions keep their own bindings. Source edits unlock after the user approves the plan (`EnterPlanMode` -> `ExitPlanMode`; outside plan mode, write the plan to a file and run `along plan approve --plan-file <path>` after the user's explicit yes). `along plan status` shows the binding.
- **Exemptions**: Read-only Q&A and 1-line micro-edits (typo fixes, comments) do not require issues.
- **Inquiry Read-Only Invariance (Zero-Mutation Rule on Questions)** [gate: require-plan-approval]: On interrogative prompts ("is X done?", "why did Y fail?"), write/modify tools are STRICTLY PROHIBITED. Return a read-only audit report and ask for confirmation before modifying anything.
- **Commit Binding** [gate: commit-issue-binding]: Every commit via `/along-commit` MUST bind to the active issue slug.
- **No AI Co-Authors**: Commit messages MUST NOT carry `Co-Authored-By:` trailers naming an AI agent (GitHub lists the vendor as a contributor). `along hook install` turns runtime attribution off; opt out via `.along/config.json` `commits.allow_ai_coauthor: true`.

## Issue Plans & Approving Ahead

- **Plan location**: An issue's plan lives next to its ticket in `.along/ISSUES/<key>/plan.md` (committed; moves with the ticket to `done/` and on rename). It is one living file: the approved baseline, then each correction appended as `## Revision N (date, source)` with a `Reason:` line. `along-team` writes its Living Plan there too; blackboards without an issue keep `.along/.session/<slug>/plan.md`.
- **Plan status** (ticket front-matter `plan_status`, shown on the board): `needs-approval` (written, waiting for the user), `approved` (ready to run), `needs-rework` (cannot be followed within the ticket). Agents may set `needs-approval` / `needs-rework`; only `along plan approve`, after the user's explicit yes, sets `approved` [gate: require-plan-approval]: a file-tool edit that sets it is denied, a shell write is reported at Stop.
- **Approve ahead**: Write the plan (plan mode, or a file), show it, and after the user's yes run `along plan approve <slug>` (`--plan-file <path>` outside plan mode) before `along start`. The issue is not started; the ticket says `plan_status: approved` and the CLI logs the approval in `.along/.session/plan-approvals.jsonl` (machine-local, closed to file tools). A later `along start <slug>`, by the user, the agent, or the orchestrator / runner daemon, runs the plan with no second approval and no re-planning (the orchestrator skips its architect).
- **Approved elsewhere**: `approved` in the ticket with no approval logged on this machine (approved on another machine, or written by hand) is not trusted: show the plan and ask once in the current channel (chat, or the daemon's Telegram reply); the orchestrator stops with `needs-input`.
- **Plans change during work; escalate only past the ticket**: Once approved, the plan belongs to the agents. A deviation they can resolve while still meeting the ticket's requirements and acceptance criteria is resolved on the spot and recorded (`along plan revise <slug> --plan-file <path> --reason "..."`); no one is asked and the status stays `approved`. Only a problem the ticket cannot absorb (a requirement cannot be met or must change, a decision only the user can make) goes to the user: `along plan rework <slug> --reason "..."`, stop, ask. In `along-team`, implementer and reviewer report plan problems to the supervisor, the architect revises, and only a ticket-level problem halts the run. Plans are not checked for staleness: a plan stays valid until the work shows otherwise.

## Entity Ecosystem

- **Entity types**: Issues (`feat`, `bug`, `debt`, `task`, `docs`, `spike`), Decisions (ADRs), Milestones, Sessions. A risk or blocker is an issue tagged `risk`; a spike is a `spike--<slug>` issue with an `## Outcome` section. Full YAML schemas: `docs/topic--domain-model.md`.
- **Canonical keys**: `<type>--<slug>` (e.g. `feat--token-refresh`). Reference by key, NEVER by file path.
- **ADRs**: Modular records in `.along/DECISIONS/ADR-YYYY-MM-DD--<slug>.md` (with legacy fallback to monolithic `DECISIONS.md`). Never edit past entries - mark superseded. Recompile projections (`.along/DECISIONS.md` board and `.along/CONSTRAINTS.md`) via `/along-decision-sync` or `along decision sync`. Create new ADRs via `/along-decision-sync` or `along decision create <slug> --title "..."`. Add terms to `.along/GLOSSARY.md`.
- **Issue lifecycle** [gate: issue-lifecycle]: Complete active issues via `along wrap <slug>` (or `along issue done <slug> --status cancelled|superseded`). Closing as done requires `validate_issue_completion` (no scaffold placeholders, mandatory Acceptance Criteria, all `- [x]` closed).
- **Entity references** [gate: entity-reference-integrity] [gate: entity-deletion-protection]: Never delete an entity other entities reference; use `along issue rename` / `along issue supersede`.
- **Auto-entity creation**: Agents MUST automatically detect user intent (build/fix/refactor -> Issue, blocked/rate-limit -> Issue tagged `risk`, compare/benchmark -> `spike` Issue, release/sprint -> Milestone) and create entities without prompting the user.

## Knowledge Base & Documentation

- **Stable Entry Point**: `README.md` and `docs/` never link into `.along/`; route through `docs/INDEX.md` or `docs/topic--<slug>.md`.
- **Portable Links**: Relative Markdown links only.
- **Fact Grounding**: Agents MUST extract facts from actual code, `README.md`, `docs/`, and `package.json`. Generic LLM placeholders are strictly prohibited.
- **Fast Retrieval**: Agents SHOULD query `/along-kb-search` before reading whole documentation files.
- **Doc Blast Radius**: After non-trivial code changes, agents MUST map affected symbols to `docs/topic--*.md` articles and update them before completing the task.
- **Manual Document Lock** [gate: doc-manual-lock]: Documents marked with `write_policy: manual` (or `locked: true`) are protected from automated agent modification during blast radius sweeps. Modifications require an explicit documentation issue (`docs--<slug>`).
- **Managed Rule Packs** [gate: rule-pack-protection]: Never edit `.along/rules/**/*.md`; `along rules attach` owns them. Project guidelines go to `docs/topic--<slug>.md` or "Project specifics"; revert with `along rules restore`. `.along/rules/gates.yaml` and `.along/scripts/` stay repo-owned.

### Documentation Routing Tree

[gate: doc-routing-compliance]

- Architectural choice / trade-off -> `.along/DECISIONS/` (ADR)
- Public overview / pitch / landing page -> `README.md`
- Technical interface contract / CLI spec -> `docs/topic--<slug>.md` (`type: reference`)
- Conceptual explanation / comparison / philosophy -> `docs/topic--<slug>.md` (`type: explanation`, `write_policy: manual`)
- Procedural walkthrough / runbook -> `docs/topic--<slug>.md` (`type: guide`)

## While Working

- **Token hygiene**: Use quiet flags (`pytest -q`, `dotnet test -v q`), filter outputs, inspect targeted line ranges.
- **Lifecycle hooks first**: Agents MUST use `/along-test`, `/along-build`, `/along-dev` (or `.along/scripts/*.py`) before raw shell commands.
- **Post-change review**: Agents MUST inspect diffs and evaluate blast radius via `along graph-impact` (or static search fallback). Silent skips are forbidden.

## Stage & Session Completion Checklist

When a stage or session completes, agents MUST execute in this order:
1. [ ] **Tests** [gate: test_before_stop]: Run via `/along-test` with quiet flags. Zero failures.
2. [ ] **File Integrity**: `git status -u` - all new/modified files non-zero size, no empty placeholders.
3. [ ] **Code Review**: Inspect diff for side effects, verify REQ-N coverage, evaluate blast radius via `along graph-impact` (or static search), verify architectural decision compliance.
4. [ ] **Entity Reconciliation**: Close issues (`done` + move to `done/`), update milestones, record the `## Outcome` of a spike. [gate: unresolved_gate_denial]: every tool call a gate denied is redone within the gate's rules or disclosed (`along gates denials`, `along gates ack <id> --note "..."`); `along wrap` / `along issue done` refuse until the user has replied to a disclosure (`--force-reason` after their reply).
5. [ ] **Doc Blast Radius**: Update affected `docs/topic--*.md`, `README.md` and Project specifics; add new terms to `.along/GLOSSARY.md` (create it on first use); touch `.along/VISION.md` only if scope/roadmap changed; run `/along-kb-sync`.
6. [ ] **Session Log & Wrap** [gate: wrap_before_stop]: `along wrap <slug> --summary "<summary>" (--decisions <ADR...> | --no-decisions)` writes `.along/SESSIONS/<YYYY>/<date>--<slug>.md` (summary, decisions, attributed `files:`, blackboard record), compiles projections, and appends to `.along/HISTORY.md` (provide `--summary` or let it fallback to issue title).
7. [ ] **Projections** [gate: projection_sync_before_stop]: Run `/along-issue-sync` and `/along-decision-sync`.
8. [ ] **HISTORY**: Verify line in `.along/HISTORY.md` (appended automatically by `along wrap`; update via `along history append <slug> "..."` if needed).
9. [ ] **Compaction**: Advise user to run `/compact`.

## Multi-Agent Routing

- **Mandatory Adaptive Complexity Escalation & Execution Mode Routing**: When scope touches > 3 files, crosses subsystems, or refactors core engines: single-agent execution is forbidden - route to `along-team`. Plans MUST declare `Execution Mode: Direct` or `Role-Based`. Role-based blackboards (`along scratch init`) are held to the step loop [gate: team-step-active] [gate: team-reviews-before-stop]; dropping it needs `along scratch fallback <slug> --reason "..."`.

## Tool-Use Rules

- **Contract-First Lifecycle**:
  - Agents MUST execute `.along/scripts/<action>.py` or `/along-test`, `/along-build`, `/along-dev` before raw shell commands.
  - When `.along/scripts/` is missing, `along test`/`along build` auto-detects and synthesizes hooks.
  - In submodules, execute the hook from that subproject's own `.along/scripts/`.
- **Environment Isolation**:
  - Agents MUST NOT install system-wide or global packages when a script fails. Fix the architecture (missing `bootstrap.ensure_deps()`, incorrect `uv` wrapper), not the environment.
- **Workspace Containment** [gate: workspace-containment]: Read and write only inside the workspace. Writes elsewhere are limited to the temp dir and runtime artifact dirs. Other repos need `allowed_roots` (`.along/rules/gates.yaml`, issue frontmatter, `along start --allow-root`). Never touch credential stores (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`).
- **Runtimes Without Along Hooks** (Claude Cowork, Cursor, OpenCode, plain shells): gates are advisory there. Agents MUST self-apply every gate-tagged rule and use the `along` CLI for tests, commits, entity changes, and wrap instead of raw tools. `along doctor` reports the enforcement level.
- **File Modification & Anti-Deletion**:
  - Never delete, truncate, or overwrite existing documentation, comments, or code unless explicitly instructed.
  - After batch edits or migrations, agents MUST run `git diff --stat` and inspect unexpected size reductions.
  - No stubs or skeletons in place of populated code.
  - Anchor edits on minimal unique chunks. Restore unintended deletions immediately.
- **Clean ASCII**: ASCII punctuation only (no typographic dashes, quotes, ellipsis, bullets, NBSP/zero-width chars or BOM); `along sanitize --write` fixes them.
- **Markdown**: Every code fence names a language.
- **Commit-time checks**: typography, code fences, links, filenames, secrets, stubs and AI co-authors are checked by `along lint` (pre-commit and CI), not while you work.
- **Bypass Is The User's Call**: `-n`, `--force-reason`, `scratch fallback` need `--reason` and the user's reply after the failure; each bypass is recorded (`along gates stats`).
- **File Content Via Tools Only** [gate: cli_safety]: Create/edit files with the agent's file tools. NEVER carry content in heredocs, `python -c`, or inline shell. Write scripts to a file first.
- **No Ad-Hoc Shell Code Probing**: Agents must never use `python -c` or inline shell commands to probe internal module symbols or inspect functions. Internal engine packages (`alongkit`, `scripts`) are not installed into the global Python environment, and ad-hoc shell probing produces confusing error traces instead of actionable information. Prescribed inspection tools: static file tools (`view_file`, `grep_search`), AST tools (`along graph-*`), official CLI subcommands (`along <command> --help`), or dedicated hermetic tests in `tests/`.
- **CLI Black-Box Invariance**: Agents MUST treat the Along CLI and development tools as strict opaque black-box executables. Reading Along engine source code (`.along/bin/*.py`, `~/.along/bin/`, `alongkit/**`, `along_*.py`) to inspect internals, arguments, or data structures is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN unless working on the Along repository itself. Always use `along <command> --help` or official documentation in `docs/`. If an Along command returns an error or fails validation, report the exact CLI error output to the user immediately. Do not attempt to reverse-engineer or debug the Along engine.
- **Verify Written Files**: After writing/patching, confirm parsing (`python -m compileall -q`, `bash -n`, etc.) before moving on.
- **Hermetic Tests**: Tests MUST target throwaway fixtures (`tempfile.mkdtemp()`), never the live repository. Read-only access to live state is allowed. Keep a meta-test that verifies `git status --porcelain -u` stays clean.
- Windows-safe filenames: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, date first.
- Keep `ISSUES.md` compact: `along context-budget --check` enforces the limit.
- Never write secrets into tracked files.

## Document: docs/topic--architecture.md (01 Architecture)

# @actdim/dynstruct-mui Architecture

## 1. System Overview

`@actdim/dynstruct-mui` provides Material UI (MUI v5/v6) component adapters specifically engineered for the `@actdim/dynstruct` component system. It bridges Material UI widgets with the dynstruct reactive component model, two-way bindings (`bind`, `bindProp`), and message bus integration.

```
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                     @actdim/dynstruct-mui                                         |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  MUI Component Adapters                                                                           |
|  - Input & Form: TextField, Select, Autocomplete, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup, Slider, Rating   |
|  - Actions: Button, IconButton, Fab, ToggleButtonGroup, SpeedDial                                 |
|  - Layout & Containers: Card, Accordion, Dialog, Drawer, Menu, List, Table, Tabs, Stepper          |
|  - Feedback & Display: Alert, Snackbar, CircularProgress, LinearProgress, Skeleton, Badge, Avatar|
|  - Navigation: Breadcrumbs, Pagination, Tooltip                                                   |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Dynstruct Integration Layer                                                                      |
|  - Hook-Constructors: useButton, useTextField, useDialog, useSelect, etc.                         |
|  - Two-way Data Binding: Seamless connection with bind(() => m.field, v => m.field = v)          |
|  - React Exports: Standard toReact() wrappers for direct JSX usage                                |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Transitive Dependency Guidelines & Invariants

No exported invariants detected across repository dependencies.

## Custom Project Dependency Hooks (`.along/scripts/dep_scan.py`)

While Along natively auto-discovers dependencies across Node.js (`package.json`), Python (`pyproject.toml`, `requirements*.txt`), .NET NuGet (`*.csproj`), Rust (`Cargo.toml`), and Go (`go.mod`), repositories using other ecosystems or internal package managers can supply a custom discovery hook:

- **Hook Path**: `.along/scripts/dep_scan.py` (or `scan_deps.py`).
- **Invocation**: `/along-dep-scan` or `along dep-scan` executes the script passing `--json` with working directory set to the project root.
- **Output Schema**: The script must write a JSON list to stdout:
  ```json
  [
    {
      "package": "custom-package",
      "ecosystem": "hex",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "files": [
        {
          "filename": "AGENTS.md",
          "path": "deps/custom-package/AGENTS.md"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
  ```
- **Monorepo Localization**: In multi-package repositories or submodules, subproject-specific hooks placed in `packages/<subproject>/.along/scripts/dep_scan.py` are executed automatically when scanning that subproject.

## Usage in Agent Sessions
When working on features involving any of the modules or external libraries above:
1. **Internal Submodules**: Follow conventions in the nearest `AGENTS.md` or subproject `docs/`.
2. **Third-Party Libraries**: Read the linked instruction files directly for framework-specific patterns and best practices.

## Document: docs/topic--domain-model.md (02 Domain Model)

# @actdim/dynstruct-mui Domain Model & Component Catalog

## 1. Domain Overview

`@actdim/dynstruct-mui` exposes typed component structures and hook-constructors wrapping `@mui/material` components.

## 2. Component Catalog

### 2.1. Form & Input Components
- **`useTextField` / `TextField`**: Material UI text field with label, helperText, error state, and two-way string binding.
- **`useSelect` / `Select`**: Select dropdown supporting single and multi-selection with options mapping.
- **`useAutocomplete` / `Autocomplete`**: Searchable combobox and autocomplete input.
- **`useCheckbox` / `Checkbox`**: Boolean checkbox toggle with label.
- **`useSwitch` / `Switch`**: On/off toggle switch.
- **`useRadioGroup` / `RadioGroup`**: Radio button selection group.
- **`useSlider` / `Slider`**: Continuous or discrete numeric slider.
- **`useRating` / `Rating`**: Star rating input widget.

### 2.2. Actions & Buttons
- **`useButton` / `Button`**: Primary, secondary, text, and contained button variants with click handlers.
- **`useIconButton` / `IconButton`**: Icon-only button wrapper.
- **`useFab` / `Fab`**: Floating Action Button.
- **`useToggleButtonGroup` / `ToggleButtonGroup`**: Segmented button group.
- **`useSpeedDial` / `SpeedDial`**: Expandable floating action speed dial.

### 2.3. Dialogs, Drawers & Layouts
- **`useDialog` / `Dialog`**: Modal dialog with title, content, actions, and open/close state.
- **`useDrawer` / `Drawer`**: Side sliding drawer container.
- **`useCard` / `Card`**: Container card with header, media, content, and action sections.
- **`useAccordion` / `Accordion`**: Expandable panel accordion.
- **`useTable` / `Table`**: Data table with sorting and pagination headers.
- **`useTabs` / `Tabs`**: Tab navigation bar.
- **`useStepper` / `Stepper`**: Multi-step wizard navigation.

### 2.4. Feedback & Indicators
- **`useAlert` / `Alert`**: Severity banner (`error`, `warning`, `info`, `success`).
- **`useSnackbar` / `Snackbar`**: Floating toast notification with auto-hide duration.
- **`useCircularProgress` / `CircularProgress`** & **`useLinearProgress` / `LinearProgress`**: Loading spinners.
- **`useSkeleton` / `Skeleton`**: Content placeholder loading skeleton.
- **`useTooltip` / `Tooltip`**: Hover tooltip popup.

## 3. Cross-Links

- [[01-[architecture](./topic--architecture.md).md]] - System Architecture

## Document: docs/topic--setup-and-workflow.md (03 Setup And Workflow)

# @actdim/dynstruct-mui Setup, Build & Storybook Workflow

## 1. Prerequisites & Installation

- **Node.js**: >= 20.0.0
- **Package Manager**: `pnpm` (version ~10.21.0)
- **TypeScript**: >= 5.9.3

Install dependencies:
```bash
pnpm install
```

### Peer Dependencies
```bash
pnpm add @actdim/dynstruct @actdim/msgmesh @actdim/utico @mui/material @emotion/react @emotion/styled react react-dom mobx mobx-react-lite
```

## 2. Scripts & Workflows

| Command | Action | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm run build` | `tsc -b tsconfig.json && vite build` | Compiles ESM packages with `.d.ts` declaration maps |
| `pnpm run storybook` | `storybook dev -p 6006` | Launches Storybook with all Material UI component stories |
| `pnpm run build-storybook` | `storybook build` | Builds static Storybook bundle |
| `pnpm run test` | `npx vitest --config=vitest.node.config.ts --no-cache` | Runs unit tests |
| `pnpm run typecheck` | `tsc -b tsconfig.json` | Runs strict TypeScript verification |
| `pnpm run lint` | `eslint "./**/*.{ts,tsx}"` | Lints codebase |
| `pnpm run format` | `prettier --write .` | Formats all files |

## 3. Storybook Catalog (`src/_stories/`)
Interactive stories exist for every wrapped Material UI component: `Button.stories.tsx`, `Dialog.stories.tsx`, `TextField.stories.tsx`, `Select.stories.tsx`, `Card.stories.tsx`, `Accordion.stories.tsx`, `Table.stories.tsx`, `Tabs.stories.tsx`, etc.

## 4. Cross-Links
- [[INDEX.md]] - Knowledge Base Root
- [[01-[architecture](./topic--architecture.md).md]] - Architecture
- [[02-[domain-model](./topic--domain-model.md).md]] - Domain Model
